title: Oikos building blocks
description: The acts every consequential thing compiles to. An Action is an ordered bundle of 1-32 blocks, applied ATOMICALLY: all or nothing. Two families: PHYSICAL acts, where the kernel checks physics (custody, funds, capacity, space, presence) and refuses what is physically impossible; and RECORD acts, which the kernel stores with their author and never judges (D19, D22). No block is ever refused for being illegal: laws are records, and entities decide what to do about them. The acting seat is bound by the orchestrator, never named in the block.

by.description: Who does the act's work, if not the actor alone (foundations F3): people, each alive, present and at work (`orchestration.performers_in`). The act's time is theirs, shared; it starts when all are free and takes effect when the last is done.

transfer.description: PHYSICAL. Move money between accounts. Only someone acting for the SOURCE account's custodian (normally its bank) can physically do this: an account holder pays by publishing an instruction to their bank. Physics: the funds exist, no overflow. The outside world's account is held in its own custody, so only those acting for the outside world can pay from it: that is how money enters the world (boundary conditions are the outside world's participants, which are world content; D31). 'settles' and 'per_instruction' link the payment to the claim it pays off and the instruction it carries out; the kernel records the links and doesn't check them.

line.description: The line of the payer's adopted budget the payment is drawn on, a label the payer gives; the kernel reads nothing into it, and a payment with none is not refused.

open_account.description: PHYSICAL. A custodian (a bank, or an entity keeping its own money) opens an account for a holder. The entity acted for becomes the custodian. Balance starts at zero.

currency.description: The account's currency; absent: the world's first. It must be one the world declares (refused otherwise: unknown_currency).

close_account.description: PHYSICAL. The custodian closes an account. Physics: the balance must be zero (money must go somewhere first). The outside world's own account can never be closed: the world's edge always exists.

construct.description: PHYSICAL. The entity acted for (the builder) begins a catalogue structure on open ground, its footprint's corner at a cell. Its materials (phase B) are taken from the builder's own holding at `materials_at` (its yard); a type with materials can't be begun without them. It completes once its build labour has been worked on it (the task `build`) and its build time has passed. No ownership is assigned: who owns it is a record. Not refused for lacking a permit or for building on someone else's land; those are matters of law.

at.description: The corner cell of the footprint: the building stands on the structure type's w x h cells from here. Refused only if a cell is off the ground, already built on, or of a terrain the type can't stand on.

materials_at.description: Where the builder keeps its materials: a structure it holds them at. Required when the type has materials.

demolish.description: PHYSICAL. The entity acted for begins bringing a structure down. Anyone still in it is displaced at once (recorded as vacated). It comes down when its type's demolition labour has been worked on it (the task `demolish`), or at once if its type needs none. Whose building it is doesn't matter to physics.

occupy.description: PHYSICAL. A body goes into a space: the acting person, or someone they bring ('who'), who must be alive and in the world. Refused only if the structure is incomplete or the space is full (its physical capacity: how many bodies could fit at all, not how many should).

vacate.description: PHYSICAL. An occupant leaves a space, or every space it's in in a structure (the acting person themselves), or is removed by someone else (eviction). Physics: the occupant is there. The kernel records who did it.

from.description: A structure (every space the occupant is in there) or one space.

create_entity.description: RECORD. Declare an organisation: gives it an id that can hold accounts, be a party and be spoken for. Whether it's recognised (registered, lawful) is interpretation. Reserved kinds 'person' and 'boundary' can't be created: bodies and the world's edge are physics. Dissolution is not a block: it's a published statement, which banks and others act on.

first_position.description: The new organisation's first position, held by the acting participant (otherwise nobody could act for it).

record_claim.description: RECORD. Record a claim: a Hohfeldian legal position. right (the counterparty has a duty, e.g. to pay), liberty (e.g. a permit to build), power (e.g. to grant permits), immunity. 'about' holds the specifics in the world's vocabulary. Anyone can record a claim; the record shows who did, for whom, and on what basis. A forged title is possible.

counterparty.description: Who bears the correlative (the duty, no-right, liability or disability). Required for financial claims.

transfer_claim.description: RECORD. Record that a claim now belongs to someone else (a sale of land, an assigned debt). Records are append-only: this adds a record referencing the claim and never edits it. Who holds a claim 'now' is read from the chain of records, and whose records to trust is interpretation.

release_claim.description: RECORD. Record that a claim is released, waived, revoked or discharged. Append-only, like transfer_claim.

propose_agreement.description: RECORD. Propose an agreement: parties and their commitments. Nothing in an agreement executes automatically. Parties (or their banks, via standing instructions) carry out commitments, and creditors record what's owed. Visible to the parties unless stated otherwise.

basis.description: What the agreement cites as its basis (e.g. a permit).

sign_agreement.description: RECORD. Sign an agreement as one of its parties. Whether the signer really had authority to sign for that party is interpretation; the record shows which participant signed, and in which position.

give_notice.description: RECORD. A party gives notice under (or in breach of) an agreement's termination terms. Whether the notice is valid is interpretation.

publish.description: RECORD. Publish a statement: a law, procedure, norm, decision, permit decision, judgment, ballot, report, budget, instruction (e.g. to a bank: pay this, keep paying this every month), dissolution notice, and so on. The kind is the world's vocabulary. Statements have no power of their own: a law is enforced, a procedure followed, an instruction executed only if some entity chooses to act on it.

data.description: Structured content for whoever acts on it: an instruction's payment details, a ballot's options, a budget's lines.

basis.description: What the statement claims its authority rests on (a vote, a constitution, a delegation).

place.description: A cell to put it up on (a sign, a notice on a fence). It's then seen by those whose channels look at that place, not through channels that look at no place. The kernel checks only that the cell exists; whether it may be put there is for the world's laws.

withdraw.description: RECORD. Record that a statement (or any record) is withdrawn, repealed or cancelled. Append-only: the original stays.

vote.description: RECORD. Cast a choice on a ballot (a published statement). Who may vote and what the result is are determined by whoever counts: the kernel only records.

message.description: VOICE. Send text to participants, positions or entities (a position's holder receives it; an entity, through those who act for it). Delivered and logged verbatim, never interpreted.

AgreementTerms.description: An agreement as a bundle of commitments (REA). Everything here is data the parties agreed to; the kernel executes none of it.

template.description: A label (lease, employment, loan, sale...) for the translator and researchers; the kernel never interprets it.

does.description: What the party commits to, in the typed vocabulary (Does).

then.description: What happens when the term runs out: absent, the agreement ends; "periodic", it continues, from one period to the next, until a party ends it by notice under its termination clauses (a fixed-term lease becoming a periodic tenancy, as tenancy law commonly provides).

Adico.description: Institutional Grammar breakdown of a statement (Crawford & Ostrom 1995). Optional structure that lets code-run institutions and measurement reason about what the text says.

or_else.description: The stated consequence, which someone would have to impose.

Formal.description: An optional machine-checkable form of a statement: a CEL condition (integer-only, allowlisted functions; see docs/research/cel-check). Never evaluated by the kernel. Code-run institutions use it to judge what they observe, measurement to find violations afterwards, the translator to warn a participant that a plan looks unlawful.

role_module.description: How a code participant does this job (opaque to the kernel; the orchestrator runs it with the holder's traits).

arrive.description: PHYSICAL. Someone crosses into the world from outside: a newcomer (name, born_at, template for their participant) or someone returning (person). Done in a position of the boundary: who comes is the outside world's business. 'carrying': money they bring, moved from the boundary's account into an account in their own custody.

born_at.description: When the newcomer was born (may be before the run: negative).

sex.description: A newcomer's biological sex, where the world models it.

variables.description: A newcomer's body variables (others start at the catalogue's initial).

leave.description: PHYSICAL. A body crosses out of the world: the acting person, or someone removed. It comes out of every space it's in; it keeps its accounts, claims and participant, and can come back.

to.description: Which of the world's edges they leave by (a boundary entity); absent: the default edge (the first). Refused otherwise: not_a_boundary.

birth.description: PHYSICAL. The acting person (as itself), alive, in the world and of an age to bear children (life.birth.ages), conceives a child, with another parent if named (who must be near: life.birth.reach). The child is born after life.birth.gestation, where the birthing parent is, occupying nothing; its participant comes from the template.

harm.description: PHYSICAL. The acting participant's own body harms someone near it (life.harm.reach). It causes an injury, whose severity, length and chance of death are drawn from life.harm. Whether anyone may do this is law.

create_position.description: A new position of the acting organisation (acting in one of its positions), vacant.

role_module.description: How a code participant does this job (opaque to the kernel; the orchestrator runs it with the holder's traits).

appoint.description: Hand one of the acting organisation's positions to a participant, or to nobody (vacating it; stepping down is appointing nobody to one's own position). Only the organisation, through a position it has, can fill its own positions: the same physical rule as custody. Whether an appointment is legitimate (an election, a charter) is for the world's records and people.

deploy.description: The supplier's act (foundations F4): the acting organisation, which supplies the template, delivers a new system from it (software, or an AI system) to a client organisation, which owns it. Anyone else is refused (`not_supplier`). What it costs is an ordinary payment to whoever supplies it, which is an agreement and a transfer, never this block.

to.description: The client organisation the system is delivered to, and belongs to. Absent: the supplier itself.

retire.description: Switch off a system participant belonging to the acting organisation, or supplied by it (a licence ended, the vendor's switch): it never acts again, and its positions fall vacant.

move_goods.description: PHYSICAL (phase B). The holder moves some of its holding of a resource to someone's holding at a place: its own elsewhere, or another's (a delivery, a handover), or out of the world to an edge. Only the holder can move its holdings (possession, D20). An edge's goods come from outside, so its holding may go negative (as for money, D31). Goods move between places instantly (a documented liberty: no transport).

from_at.description: Where the goods are now: a structure, or for an edge, itself.

to_at.description: Where they go: a structure, or for an edge, itself.

work.description: PHYSICAL (phase B). Work: `units` of a task, at a structure, by performers who are there (in a space of the task's kind), alive and present, each with time left in today's working day; the units' labour is shared evenly among them. The task's inputs come from the actor's holding at the structure, its outputs go to it, and its changes to state variables of `on` (or of `at`). The built-in tasks `build` and `demolish` work on a structure (`on`) begun or coming down. Who works for whom is content (agreements), never physics (D20): the kernel checks only that the performers are there, and their hours exist.

on.description: Or a person at the place, or a space of it (everyone in it): the task's on_body applies to each body.

survey.description: A survey (a task that `surveys`): of a species or a field, in these cells, one unit each. Only the actor learns the estimates (the outcome's `surveyed`).

investigate.description: An investigation (a task that investigates): of goods of a kind taken from someone, at a structure.

Outcome.description: What a commitment comes to, in the world's own terms (VISION 15): one of these. The same vocabulary for agreements, offers and practices, and the one the call language already writes. The kernel executes none of it; of an agreement it checks only that a place named to be or to work at is one (`not_a_place`).

line.description: The line of the payer's adopted budget the payment is drawn on, a label the payer gives (a payment with none is not refused).

quantity.description: A whole number as a decimal string (0 allowed): a quantity in a commitment.

in.description: A building, or a space in one. An agreement that names anything else here is refused at the act (`not_a_place`).

at.description: Where the work is done: a building, or a space in one. An agreement that names anything else here is refused at the act (`not_a_place`).

units.description: A whole number as a decimal string (0 allowed): a quantity in a commitment.

Does.description: What a party commits to: an outcome in the typed vocabulary, or anything else in words. (Before contracts 0.5 was typed, this was free-form data: a convention only code could read.)

Eligibility.description: Who may take something up or take part: every condition given must hold; none given means anyone.

dealing_with.description: Party to an agreement in force with this entity: its tenant, its worker, its member, its customer. Eligibility by something other than membership of anything (docs/behaviour/founding.md).

Offer.description: What someone may take up, on what terms, and how: facts in the world's terms, never what it's worth to anyone (docs/design/ai-citizens.md 2a). It has no power: taking it up is an act like any other, and the offerer may still decline.

take_up.description: How: sign an agreement on these terms, apply (a form, a post), order, join (a membership), attend (a practice).

per.description: For each unit taken (an order's price per item).

then.description: As an agreement's terms: "periodic", it continues after its term until ended by notice.

available.description: How many can take it up (a posting 1, a home 1, a shop's stock).

practice.description: The practice it's for (take_up: attend or join).

hears.description: What the offerer hears (take_up: apply): the matters a desk, a list, a tribunal or a group takes up, so that someone with a grievance of that kind can find it by what it says and not by its name (docs/behaviour/frictions.md). Facts only: it has no power; nothing is heard unless someone applies, and nothing follows unless the offerer acts and whoever it names obeys.

about.description: The matter: a kind of paper (a notice, a bill, a decision) or of thing gone wrong, in the world's own labels.

can.description: What it may do about one: order (binding words, if obeyed or enforced), recommend, mediate (bring the two together), refer (pass it to whoever must act), represent (take it up with the other side for the applicant), publish (make it known).

undoes.description: It may set a paper of this kind aside.

form.description: The kind of statement an application is made on (none: `application`).

within.description: How long it says it takes to answer.

Practice.description: A recurring situation people take part in: a service, a meeting, a market, a class (Versu's social practices; docs/design/ai-citizens.md 2b). Facts only; it has no power: nothing happens unless people come and do what they choose.

at.description: Where: a space, or a cell.

Registry.description: A registry's act (docs/design/rebuild.md 7.5): an organisation registered or dissolved, as a registrar records it publicly. Content, never physics: the kernel stores it and judges nothing.

Assertion.description: Something put forward to be believed (docs/design/contracts-0.7.md A1, named `assertion` because `claim` is already a legal position in these contracts): what's asserted, in words, and optionally whom or what it's about. Facts only: no stated truth and no power; whether anyone believes it is theirs.

take.description: Taking goods another holds at a structure where the taker is, without their consent (world-expansion 7.3). Recorded as it happened (taken); the holder sees their holding fall; nobody is told who.

connection.description: An act on a connection (foundations-2 C3, law 8; docs/nothing-from-nothing.md). Its operator (the holder of the supply whose tree the node is on) opens one (`open` with `kind`, `node`, `to`, `at`, `rate`; or, naming a closed `connection`, opens it again), closes it, interrupts or restores it; its user or its operator sets its rate (`set`). The kernel stores the supply contracts and never reads them.

link.description: An act on a link by its operator: shut it, open it, reclose it after it tripped, or put it on a rotation (a standing schedule: off for `off` seconds of every `every`, counted from `from`; `off` nought ends it). Only the act is logged; the schedule's effects are state.
